newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth confirms bid for Peru's Tele 2000.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth confirms bid for Peru's Tele 2000.

text.p: BellSouth Corp on Tuesday confirmed that it was offering $1.50 per share for 54 to 64 percent of Peruvian cellular phone company Tele 2000.
A 54 percent stake would cost $100 million, it said.
The Lima Stock Exchange announced the BellSouth tender offer on Monday. Shareholders of Tele 2000 have 10 business days to tender their shares.
BellSouth has agreed to buy 38 percent of Tele 2000 from two major shareholders, including Tele 2000 Chairman Genaro Delgado Parker.
If BellSouth's tender offer is successful, BellSouth and Parker would jointly hold 90 percent or more of Tele 2000.

Tele 2000 shares closed at 3.80 soles ($1.47) on the Lima bourse on Monday. The bourse said the BellSouth offer worked out to 4.00 soles per share, based on an exchange rate of 2.67 soles per dollar. On Tuesday Tele 2000 shares were 0.10 soles higher at 3.90 at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.

The bourse said BellSouth, a U.S. regional Bell, had been negotiating with Tele 2000 for more than a year. Tele 2000 holds cellular rights to serve Lima and portions of western Peru. It also provides cable TV and paging.
A spokesman for BellSouth said this would be the company's sixth Latin American wireless market. It already has stakes in companies in Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, Venezuela and Panama.
